newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAA orders two 747s after long delays.
newsitem.headline: SAA orders two 747s after long delays.

text.p: South African Airways announced on Monday it was buying two additional Boeing 747-400s powered by Rolls-Royce engines, ending months of uncertainty about the order.
The aircraft are due to be delivered in May and October 1998.
But airline spokesman Leon Els said SAA was still considering whether to proceed with an option for seven Boeing 777s. "The order for the 777s has not been finalised," he said.
State-run SAA initially placed the order for the nine aircraft in November 1995 but the Department of Trade and Industry baulked at the cost of the engine contracts, delaying the project.
SAA chief executive Mike Myburgh said in a statement on Monday that the new Rolls-Royce powered aircraft were needed to meet the increased passenger traffic betwen South Africa and the Unted States.

"The RB211-powered 747-400 fleet has played an important part in servicing an area of significant traffic growth; we are increasing both the number and frequency of our routes to the U.S. for which the new aircraft will play a vital role."
